programs.title: Health Data Rights on the Blockchain: A Worker Education Series
outcomes: Explain how encrypted health data exchange and smart-contract access controls affect workplace benefits and privacy
Interpret a DAO governance workflow and identify where member voice enters decisions
Recognize fraud-detection and compliance alerts that protect member funds

sessions.activity: Hands-on walkthrough of SMS-based patient consent and encrypted data sharing, role-playing patient, provider and Health Agent perspectives.
Mock DAO session: members review a Finance Agent fraud alert, debate a resource-allocation proposal and record outcomes without touching human-reserved votes.
Guided exploration of how a Security Agent monitors cross-network transactions (Ethereum, Hyperledger, Polkadot, Cosmos) and what members can and cannot see.
Panel discussion with R&D Agent demonstrations on ALS and Parkinson's compound modeling, focused on jobs, safety and worker questions.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized post-session quiz scores and consent-workflow exercise outcomes (no personal health data) aggregated to improve union training materials.
programs.consent: Voluntary participation with signed digital consent; any example data is synthetic; no member health or biometric data is collected; withdrawal deletes contributions.

programs.title: BioDAO Explorers: Genes, Blocks and Bay Mud
outcomes: Describe how AI helps model therapies for rare diseases like ALS and Parkinson's
Explain simply how a blockchain ledger keeps records verifiable
Connect the Oyster Point coastal setting to why location matters for biotech campuses

sessions.activity: Age-appropriate intro to molecular modeling: students use bead-and-paper models to see how the R&D Agent screens compounds for neurodegenerative diseases.
Unplugged blockchain game: teams link paper 'blocks' across four colored ledgers to understand verified cross-network data.
Privacy scenario cards: students decide who should see a patient's data and act out SMS consent with the Health Agent concept.
Classroom DAO: students propose and discuss a class project; teachers model human-only final votes per the 'Agents operate; people govern' rule.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized pre/post concept-quiz scores and aggregated lesson feedback only; no student names, identifiers or personal data.
programs.consent: Signed guardian/parent consent forms required before participation; teachers act as data stewards; all data aggregated and de-identified; parents may opt out at any time and contributions are removed.

programs.title: Transparent Health Data Stewardship with DAOs
outcomes: Apply DAO governance frameworks to multi-stakeholder health programs
Design consent-first data sharing using smart contracts and SMS consent
Assess cross-jurisdiction compliance needs with the Compliance Agent model

sessions.activity: Workshop mapping an NGO program onto DAO structures: which decisions stay human-reserved, which flows agents can automate.
Case-lab drafting smart-contract access rules and SMS consent scripts for community health data sharing.
Comparison exercise across Ethereum, Hyperledger, Polkadot and Cosmos ledgers for verified, interoperable program records.
Structured dialogue on biopharma agent roles (R&D, Clinical Support) and where NGO community voices plug in.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized workshop templates and de-identified case outcomes shared across participating NGOs to build a common DAO-governance practice library.
programs.consent: Facilitators obtain organizational and individual consent before any case data is used; all shared material is de-identified and reviewed by program leads before release.

programs.title: Blockchain for Rare-Disease Nonprofits: From Lab to Ledger
programs.grade_or_level: Board and program staff / introductory professional
outcomes: Understand how AI-driven personalized therapy pipelines serve ALS and Parkinson's communities
Explain blockchain transparency for donations and program records
Build a patient-consent-first data policy for nonprofit health programs

sessions.activity: Guided tour of AI compound optimization for rare diseases, with discussion of what nonprofit advocates should ask researchers.
Donation-tracing exercise: follow a simulated gift across interoperable ledgers to see verifiable, auditable records.
Draft a community data policy covering encrypted sharing, smart-contract access and SMS patient consent.
Simulated nonprofit DAO meeting: discuss budget reallocation using Finance Agent alerts; humans retain all final decisions.
Closing roundtable connecting nonprofit missions to biopharma agent roles and partnership questions for future planning.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized policy drafts and aggregated exercise results contributed to a shared open library of nonprofit blockchain-governance templates.
programs.consent: Individual consent collected for any shared material; patient scenarios are synthetic; no real beneficiary health data is used; organizations may withdraw contributions at any time.
